notes: This file is the single source. The pack renders it and the check enforces it, so the two cannot drift.
A rule with claimOnly:true is skipped on a line that ends in a question mark. A question is not a claim, and a FAQ has to be able to ask the question it answers.
A rule with copyOnly:true is skipped on a surface whose kind is 'code'. Identifiers, column names and MetricValue states are not front-facing copy.

Surface scope 'blockquote' means only markdown blockquote lines are checked. In an evidence document the copy is what is inside the quote; the prose around it is the rule, and a rule has to be able to name the word it forbids.
Surface scope 'file' checks every line. Punctuation rules never run on scope 'file' because source code is full of exclamation marks and no-break-space arithmetic that are not copy.

rules.why: D-001.16 forbids an unconditional promise that the service or a hosted artifact will exist. The trap already caught this programme once (R-008, D-021).
rules.substitute: for as long as you stay / for as long as the agreement renews continuously without lapse / read-only, for as long as the service exists

rules.why: D-016. No solicitor and no accountant reviewed anything on this programme, and nothing may imply otherwise.
Compliance is a continuing obligation and a contested judgement, not a state a company can assert about itself.
rules.substitute: Name the artifact, then E09.10 section 6 Answer 1.

rules.why: D-020. There is no allotment in the commercial terms and nothing to reconcile. E09.01 section 4.1 retires these names permanently.
rules.substitute: Every couple who books their wedding with you gets a workspace, for as long as your licence is current.

rules.why: E09.10 section 5 P6 blocks 'unlimited' and 'no seats' in shipped copy until R-016's code changes land. Its stated basis is now stale and the residual defect is different from the one it names. Recorded as OQ-6 in E09.11 section 14; the gate is not lifted by this file.
rules.substitute: The P5 sentence, which is true today and does not use the word.

rules.why: D-010.2 and D-022. The bare figure describes a product we deliberately do not ship, and the failure it hides is a couple losing access before their own wedding at the venue that gifted it.
rules.substitute: 18 months from when the couple opens it, or 3 months past the wedding, whichever is later.

rules.why: R-017. Dietary and allergy data reveals health and routinely reveals religious belief; accessibility requirements reveal disability. Entered by the couple about guests who never agreed to anything.
D-021. Both prices are VAT-inclusive in every agreement, order form, invoice and page.
rules.substitute: including VAT at the prevailing rate

rules.why: The place is held 14 days, once, extendable by the founder personally. That is a fact, stated once, plainly.
rules.substitute: Your place is held for 14 days.

rules.why: Venue branding at launch is the venue's name only. No logo, no venue-written welcome message, no venue-controlled colour or theme in the couple's workspace.
rules.substitute: The venue's name, one quiet line. Not a logo wall.

rules.why: The venue-visible list is exactly invitation administration, activation evidence and aggregate adoption evidence. A fourth thing named in copy is a copy defect and probably a product defect.
patterns: \bthe venue sees what the couple chooses to share\b

rules.why: The master never-list, plus the whole of BRAND.md section 3.
Aggregate is the product, not a presentation choice. There is no biggest user, no per-couple row, no ranking, no leaderboard.
rules.substitute: Not enough activity to report yet.
rules.patternNote: The last pattern is claim-shaped on purpose. 'no ranking and no list of who is behind' is the approved negation from E11.11 section 2, and a bare 'who is behind' pattern flags the sentence that exists to promise the opposite.

rules.why: Banned in all front-facing copy. Comma, colon or full stop. Title separators use a middot.
No exclamation marks. Anywhere. Confidence does not shout.

citationNote: A line that forbids a word is not a line that uses it, and a voice guard listing the banned register has to be able to list it.

Every exemption is explicit. There is no heuristic. The first version of this guard was a heuristic (a quoted match on a line carrying a prohibition word) and it suppressed two REAL defects on the live venues page, because ordinary copy is full of 'no' and 'not'.
Each entry names its line by a distinctive substring, never by a line number. Reword the line and the exemption stops matching and the hit comes back, which is the correct failure direction.
The check prints the citation count per surface on every run, so an exemption cannot be quiet.
